chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Hodges sitting in at the Saratoga Sunday matinee
summary: The Sunday matinee was the only time the Saratoga had a crowd, and Hodges would come in and Holmes would invite him up to play.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I see. Well, while you were with Russell at the Saratoga Club, you have mentioned that Hodges used to come in sometimes and sit in for you...

No, not often. He did come in. He come into the matinee on Sunday. That was the only time they had a crowd in there. They had a matinee on Sunday' which was leased out to a private club. And they'd run this Sunday matinee dance with younger people, you know. That's the only time we had a crowd in there.
So naturally, Hodges would come in. All different musicians would come in. And Hodges, naturally, I'd ask him to come up and play for me. And he'd be glad to. He loved to blow anyway.
